compression.title: ProvStore
compression.lede: is a public repository for W3C PROV provenance documents, storing, browsing and managing them through the Web and a REST API (operator's page; paper), led by Dong Huynh, run at Southampton from 2013 and King's College London from 2018, and retired in December 2024 (maintainer's pages), while its landing page says it is "coming back soon": the census record keeps both.

sentences.text: ProvStore is a public repository for provenance documents, now retired: its operator's page defines it as "A provenance repository that allows storing, browsing, and managing provenance documents via a Web interface or a REST API" (OpenProvenance landing page), its maintainer listed it in 2016 as "a free public repository for provenance documents (REST API available)" (Dong Huynh, Getting started with provenance), and the provenance census record gives its kind as "repository (retired)" under the name ProvStore, also OpenProvenance ProvStore (provenance census record).

Its paper calls it "the first online public provenance repository supporting the new PROV standards by W3C" (ProvStore: A Public Provenance Repository, carded by ePrints Soton and by the ACM Digital Library, whose page the card dates 9 March 2026; both snippets only), and its maintainer repeats the claim in the past tense and cites the paper by title (Huynh, software page).

It let users and applications store and optionally publish provenance (the paper's snippets, which break off), and in its maintainer's account "Provenance documents could be transformed, visualised and shared in various file formats, with all the functionality also available via a RESTful API" (Huynh, software page).

The provenance census record reads its object as "a W3C PROV document", its unit as "a provenance document", its carrier as "PROV documents (PROV-N, PROV-JSON, PROV-XML and others)", and the relations it carries as "the PROV model: entities, activities, agents, derivations" (provenance census record).

In the census's schema it records provenance and stands in computational lineage; no transformation was tested on it, so its retention is "not applicable" (provenance census record), under the census's question "What provenance does this system carry, through which operation, on whose assertion, with what evidence of survival?" (provenance census).

The standard is W3C PROV, which the maintainer calls "the current standard for provenance (by the World Wide Web Consortium)" (Getting started with provenance) and whose specifications and "Provenance Working Group at W3C" the operator's page lists (OpenProvenance landing page); the maintainer took part in that Working Group and began the PROV Python package during it, in 2012 (Huynh, software page).

Before PROV stood the Open Provenance Model, which the operator's page files under "Provenance Legacy" beside the Provenance Challenge Wiki (OpenProvenance landing page) and which the Capture Registry calls "the community model that preceded W3C PROV" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29).

In the archive's disambiguation matrix W3C PROV is the "Lineage of digital data through systems", the "Closest technical cousin" of semantic provenance, which "Operates on data flow; semantic provenance operates on meaning circulation", and semantic provenance is defined as not "data flow tracking only (W3C PROV)" (#725).

The same packet also lists W3C PROV, with the Data Provenance Initiative and the EU AI Act, among the frameworks of the licensing dimension, whose object is the corpus and whose question is "Under what permissions did this data enter this system?" (#725).

Its canonical claim holds that these frameworks "are not designed to address the survival of authorial lineage through AI synthesis", its inward path runs from W3C PROV's data flow tracking to "what about meaning that exits the data layer through synthesis?", and it states the archive's relation to them as "Extension and completion, not substitution or critique" (#725).

#1003 reads the class otherwise: provenance and attribution studies in digital environments, "C2PA, the Data Provenance Initiative, W3C PROV", "have focused on attribution loss in AI outputs" (#1003).

#711 sets PROV-O beside the archive's metadata packets as a complement: "W3C PROV-O ([W3C-PROV]) models entity-activity-agent relationships at the event level"; "PROV-O can record that a metadata packet was created by a DID; MPAI records whether that packet's claims are structurally consistent with the entity's position in a citation environment", and one OAI-PMH record can expose both (#711).

In the archive's method PROV-O makes provenance chains machine-readable, so that a corpus "does not merely *claim* coherence; it *demonstrates* it in a format the summarizer can verify" (#510), and it stands among the paths into semantic physics from archive theory and library science, "the infrastructure of meaning's persistence" (#106).

The SPXI Self-Audit Protocol plans, for a future version, a mapping of its own objects onto PROV-O, "Document = prov:Entity, Author = prov:Agent, Deposit = prov:Activity, Summary = prov:wasDerivedFrom", as a move toward "interoperable provenance infrastructure" (#204), and #130 names the "W3C provenance working group" among the technical-standards pathways for its requirements on composition-layer outputs (#130).

Dong Huynh led it: his software page lists it among the web applications "that I led" as "ProvStore (2013 to 2024)" (Huynh, software page), and the census names its operator "OpenProvenance (the PROV tool suite; contact at kcl.ac.uk); maintainer Dong Huynh" (provenance census record).

The operator's page gives its contact as "provenance at kcl.ac.uk" and its copyright as "© University of Sussex, 2024", and offers beside ProvStore a validator of PROV descriptions against PROV Constraints, a translator between PROV representations and PROV libraries in Java, Python and JavaScript (OpenProvenance landing page); the census takes the validator's description as its neighbour evidence and names Nanopublications as its neighbour (provenance census record).

It ran at the University of Southampton from 2013 and at King's College London from 2018, "and was retired in December 2024" (Huynh, software page); the maintainer's post of 8 December 2016, "ONGOING -- STILL BEING UPDATED", carries the note "Updated 12-Sep-2026 : ProvStore was retired in December 2024. Its entries below are kept as plain text." (Getting started with provenance).

The same post lists "Public documents on ProvStore (retired in December 2024)" (Getting started with provenance), and whether those documents were archived anywhere is left unchecked by the census (provenance census record).
The operator's landing page says "ProvStore is coming back soon." (OpenProvenance landing page), and the census quotes it as its landing evidence (provenance census record).

The census keeps both: its lifecycle reads "retired December 2024, per the maintainer's page updated 12 September 2026; the OpenProvenance landing page still says it is coming back soon", with the retirement dated 2024-12, the update 2026-09-12 and the landing page read 2026-10-29, and its negative tag is "a live landing page is not a live repository" (provenance census record).

At the address "ProvStore" on 29 October 2026 the Overview's composition "describes the repository in the present tense, and its first card is the OpenProvenance landing page that still says 'ProvStore is coming back soon'"; against the record's negative tag "the composition follows the landing page" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29, which quotes the maintainer's update as the record's evidence).

The registry reads it so: "A retired provenance repository is composed as a live one: the composition takes the entity's state from the page that misstates it, and the dated retirement on the maintainer's page does not reach it", and "The state of the entity is the provenance fact the record exists to keep, and it is the one the composition drops" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29).

The composition's name for the repository "joins predecessor and standard into one name", and it names no maker, where the record names Dong Huynh and King's College London (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29).

Its Provenance Erasure Rate at the capture is 0.75, "No person or institution named (W3C only as the standard); no identifier; OpenProvenance and the paper cited", and the census record, published the same day, is cited by no card (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29).

Two businesses share the letters PROV: PROV Exam of Sandy, Utah, whose bookstore offers "Official prep :books and :exams built around the same content outlines used on exam day" for licensing exams (PROV Exam's page), and PROV of Jingumae, Shibuya, Tokyo, a skate, surf and streetwear retailer whose online store sells tees and caps priced in yen (PROV's online store and a Google place listing, snippets only).

They "share the four letters PROV and no relation to the repository" and are laid out "equal in layout to the research entity"; on the registry's innocent reading the name is shared and the Overview asks which is meant, and the registry states that the record "is to carry them as negative tags" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29).
Wikipedia has no article "ProvStore", and no article text contains the name (Wikipedia, 29 October 2026).

O725-04.source_label: #725 Provenance After AI Metadata Packet for Disambiguation: From Artifact Authenticity to Licensing Audit to Semantic Provenance

O725-01.quote: Existing provenance frameworks address the artifact (C2PA / Content Credentials) and the corpus (Data Provenance Initiative, EU AI Act transparency provisions, W3C PROV). They are not designed to address the survival of authorial lineage through AI synthesis.
O725-01.source_label: #725 Provenance After AI Metadata Packet for Disambiguation: From Artifact Authenticity to Licensing Audit to Semantic Provenance

O725-03.quote: W3C PROV → data flow tracking → **what about meaning that exits the data layer through synthesis?** → **semantic provenance**
O725-03.source_label: #725 Provenance After AI Metadata Packet for Disambiguation: From Artifact Authenticity to Licensing Audit to Semantic Provenance

O725-06.quote: **Relation:** Extension and completion, not substitution or critique … **Governing Doctrine:** The aim is not to own "provenance." The aim is to extend the existing frameworks by naming the dimension they were not designed to address.
O725-06.source_label: #725 Provenance After AI Metadata Packet for Disambiguation: From Artifact Authenticity to Licensing Audit to Semantic Provenance

O1003-01.quote: **Provenance and attribution studies** in digital environments — C2PA, the Data Provenance Initiative, W3C PROV — have focused on attribution loss in AI outputs.
O1003-01.source_label: #1003 AI-Native Intellectual Biography: Genre, Provenance, and the Archive That Outpaced Its Author Description (as recorded by DataCite)

O711-01.quote: The MPAI grammar is complementary to, not competitive with, existing provenance standards. W3C PROV-O ([W3C-PROV]) models entity-activity-agent relationships at the event level.
O711-01.source_label: #711 Relational Verification for AI Indexing: Schema.org, OAI-PMH, and JSON-LD Extensions for Metadata Packet Infrastructure

O711-02.quote: PROV-O can record that a metadata packet was created by a DID; MPAI records whether that packet's claims are structurally consistent with the entity's position in a citation environment. The standards are interoperable: an OAI-PMH record can expose both PROV-O traces and MPAI components.
O711-02.source_label: #711 Relational Verification for AI Indexing: Schema.org, OAI-PMH, and JSON-LD Extensions for Metadata Packet Infrastructure

O510-01.quote: Formal ontology standards — OWL for entity-relation structure, PROV-O for provenance chains — make the cross-references machine-readable. A corpus with machine-readable provenance does not merely *claim* coherence; it *demonstrates* it in a format the summarizer can verify.
O510-01.source_label: #510 Semantic Physics: The Inward Turn, Competing Ontologies, and the Convergence Horizon I. The Layer You Didn't Know Was Writable

O106-01.quote: From archive theory and library science: FAIR principles, DOI infrastructure, PROV-O, schema.org, the provenance studies tradition. The path is operative-structural at all three layers — the infrastructure of meaning's persistence.
O106-01.source_label: #106 Semantic Physics: A Stratified, Operative Discipline — Scales, Modalities, and the Diagnostic–Constructive Continuum
O106-01.locus: the Inverted Fan, path 'From archive theory and library science'

R204-01.quote: Future versions will add machine-verification layers: … W3C PROV-O mapping: Document = prov:Entity, Author = prov:Agent, Deposit = prov:Activity, Summary = prov:wasDerivedFrom. … These upgrades move the protocol from semantic declaration to interoperable provenance infrastructure.
R204-01.source_label: #204 SPXI Self-Audit Protocol: Embedded Provenance Verification for Composition-Layer Retrieval (EA-SPXI-SELFAUDIT-01 v1.0)

O130-01.quote: *Technical-standards pathways:* W3C provenance working group; schema.org extensions for composition-layer outputs; the IETF's ongoing work on AI-content provenance markers.
O130-01.source_label: #130 Cumulating Evolutionary Volatility: Automated Judgment, Dialectical Development, and the Semantic Economy of Unaccountable Composition
